input.summary:
room: ground gallery now builds with no REFUSED writes and no OFF-PALETTE blocks: the part places 48 blocks and make.sh writes build.nbt (exit 0).
The fix: x47 is dropped from the centre-line hanging-lantern loop, because the colonnade's porchLantern already hangs a chandelier there (lantern y8, chain y9). Left alone, my loop wrote a lantern at y7 under it, floating with no chain.
Only parts/room-29.mjs was edited.
left: The whole build still reports REFUSED writes from other parts (entrance hall, parlour library, dining room, pantry, powder room, kitchen, bedroom 3, bedroom 5, bedroom 6, cottage bath, gazebo, greenhouse). Those belong to their own parts and were not touched.

make.sh still reports OFF-PALETTE blocks in the roof part (tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, polished_deepslate_*, stone_brick_slab, etc.). They come from roof.json, not this part.
The x47 centre-line chandelier is now the colonnade's porchLantern alone; the room lane looks right only if that part keeps its lantern at y8 and chain at y9.

waste.what: Working out which refused cell belonged to which earlier part, and whether my extra lantern at y7 also collided, was done by reading the coordinate loops by hand.
waste.cost: One Read of the module plus two full make.sh runs (about 40 refusal lines to scan)
waste.tool: A conflict pre-check, e.g. `mcd plan`/`runParts` option that lists every cell the part would write that an earlier part owns (with the owning part's name) before any write. Or a layers() option `skipOccupied: true` that drops those cells and reports them as a count.

waste.what: The stacked lantern at y7 under the existing chandelier was not caught as a floating hanging block until a re-run; I found it by reasoning about the chain and lantern placement.
waste.cost: One extra reasoning pass plus the fix
waste.tool: `$MCD check build.nbt` already reports hanging lanterns with nothing above; running it on the part's own output (or a check hook in runParts) would have flagged the y7 lantern before the first make.sh run.
